# Deployment Requirements Quality Checklist: GitHub Pages Deployment

**Purpose**: Review the GitHub Pages deployment requirements for completeness, clarity, consistency, and readiness for implementation.
**Created**: 2026-09-20
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are the deployment trigger conditions for production and non-production branches explicitly defined to match the issue acceptance criteria? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are the build and publication prerequisites for GitHub Pages clearly stated so reviewers can assess deployability without hidden assumptions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are the repository-specific hosting assumptions and base-path requirements documented in the requirements rather than implied? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are the issue acceptance criteria preserved in requirement language without introducing additional scope beyond the documented feature? [Traceability, Spec §Acceptance Criteria]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 - Is the meaning of "production branch" and "feature branch" unambiguous across all requirements and user stories? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is "build is deployable" stated with objective review criteria rather than a vague or implied expectation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is the GitHub Pages base-path requirement defined in a way that can be checked by reviewers without hidden deployment assumptions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 - Do the user stories and functional requirements align on the single-source production deployment model? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 1, §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK009 - Are deployment and branch isolation requirements consistent with the repository branching policy and issue-driven workflow? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Constitution §4]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are the content and hosting expectations consistent with the project’s static-site purpose and GitHub Pages target? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 - Are the success criteria measurable enough to verify the site is live and asset paths resolve correctly? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK012 - Are the success criteria framed in user-visible outcomes instead of implementation detail? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK013 - Can the deployment requirement be reviewed without embedding implementation details such as specific action names or deployment engine internals? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-005]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 - Are primary, alternate, and exception deployment scenarios covered for both production and non-production branches? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1, §User Story 2, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 - Are the failure or zero-state scenarios for invalid base-path configuration or branch misuse explicitly considered? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 - Are responsive UX and accessibility considerations addressed where public deployment affects mobile and desktop users? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK017 - Are content integrity and brand accuracy expectations addressed for published site content? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK018 - Are accessibility expectations for public-facing content and navigation specified as requirement-quality concerns rather than assumed to be covered by implementation? [Non-Functional, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are responsive behavior expectations across mobile, tablet, and desktop covered at the requirement level for public deployment readiness? [Non-Functional, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are assumptions about GitHub Pages compatibility, hosting constraints, and deployment boundaries documented and reviewable? [Dependencies & Assumptions, Spec §Assumptions]

## Dependencies & Ambiguities

- [ ] CHK021 - Are any remaining domain assumptions or exclusions clearly documented rather than hidden behind implied defaults? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are there any unresolved requirement ambiguities around acceptable deployment entry points or release approval gates that should be clarified before implementation? [Ambiguity, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` is maintained separately by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Use the checklist to review the written requirements, not to verify feature implementation.
